answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents must stake assets across a dense trust topology. A game-theoretic multi-agent auditing protocol detects sparse topological cuts between honest clusters and any dense nebula of colluding clones. When verifiers catch invalid claims, the malicious stake is subjected to slashing, while a secretive whisper network flags cut discrepancies. Because expanding duplicate identities demands superlinear attacker cost across multiple cut verifications, orchestrating an undetectable counterfeit swarm remains an impossible fable.
